conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and downtrending holdings. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting around ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech and broad indices. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Add to SOXL, SPAL, and MUU, increasing leveraged ETF exposure to press high-scoring setups.
Trim QQQI to 15% to free up capital for higher-growth opportunities.

aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets a higher ~4%/month return by leaning into leveraged ETFs and concentrated positions. Be aware that this significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs experience daily decay and rebalancing, meaning losses can accumulate very quickly, especially in volatile markets. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero to eliminate high-risk exposure.
Sell SMH and CRWD to reduce high-beta sector and single-name exposure.
Increase QQQI to 30% to boost monthly distribution potential.

This plan focuses on generating steady income with minimal growth.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting around ~1%/month in distributions. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income and broad index ETFs. While distributions are sought, they are variable and NAV can still fall in market selloffs; this is not a savings account.
